items.note: Story 1: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president 1889-1911, creamery built 1891
Article VII quoted: pounds of butterfat found by test, not weight of milk; 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern'
Falke's point given: under payment by weight nothing that followed would have cost any man a dollar
Loomis secretary from 1901, Teague bookkeeper, Sill buttermaker at Larrow Green - all three inside Section A
Nowhere in the eight reconstructions is Selby Vose called Gideon's son or dated manager from 1913; both appear only in B3/D3, and credit does not travel into A from B-G
Story 5 gives the station-gain line, its three-figure shape, five and a quarter per cent, carried to the general account (the 1905-origin claim is charged as a corruption deduction instead)
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896 on Sill's bench glass from Larrow Green
Weighed in, samples composited over ten days, charge drawn to the mark, per-cent neck read against the rulings, cream down / skim back
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897
Invoice reproduced in full: 6 doz. pipettes 17.6 c.c., 12 doz. bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, total 77.93
Story 3: the same 0.19 in the flush of June as in the depth of February, in wet years and dry
Section A describes pipette manufacture but never says the pipette cannot be checked without a burette / that none existed in the county; that argument appears only in F1
Ansel Keddie b.1861, tester from the 4 May 1896 opening for twenty-nine seasons, put out 30 April 1925, died Feb 1934
Bench routine (5:30, compositing, charge, acid, dividers, thirty-one times a week for twenty-nine seasons) and the test book in his own hand, five columns
Both figures (3.61 station average, 3.80 on borrowed/true glass) are inside Section A; the key credits the two figures anywhere in A without requiring the leaf to be printed
Story 4: broke 8 May, borrowed measure to 10 July, nine weeks at 3.80, back to 3.61 the day the station's measure returned, his own question mark
Story 6: Orra Brant, Emmet's sister, married Ansel in 1889; Emmet the largest hauler; the irony stated
1919 water circular over the manager's own signature; the 17 March 1925 statement quoted verbatim
Died Feb 1934 still under the imputation ('not one said the other thing'); test book to the Historical Rooms in 1959
Hessel Bottom wet ground, six farms, Emmet Brant the largest piece
Two-column weigh book from 1 January 1897; the columns always agreed, so the weighing was never at fault

1902 complaints given, but the item's gate fails: Story 3 sets 3.61 against Larrow Green's 3.78 and then calls 'the deficiency' 0.19, and E8 treats Roy Brant's 0.17 as a wrong value resolved to 0.19 - the visible gap and the true shortfall are conflated
1908 Grigg committee, Jan-Feb-Mar sampling named, hay conclusion reported as the committee's finding and rejected
200,000 lb even on a recorded test of 3.42 (Story 6); proportional loss with 3.42 short 0.18 and 4.56 short 0.24 (Story 3)
To Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958 and returned, to Hazel 1962, Historical Rooms 1963
Alder Corners Cheese Co., over Redlow Ridge, Vessey County, built by Jerome Cudd (year does not gate; the 1913 assertion is charged as a deduction)
From 1915 four of the six Bottom men hauled over the ridge from about 1 June to mid-September and to Ostrey Hollow otherwise; commercial reason given
REQUIRED met with all four elements: another county, his own bench, his own glassware, and a book never compared with anybody's
Story 6 gives 1915-1930, sixteen seasons, 3.78-3.82 averaging 3.80; Story 8 states the same milk ran about 0.19 higher across the ridge (the 'fourteen' slip is charged as a deduction)

Same four men's milk off the same wet ground tested 3.80 on another man's bench ('Good milk off wet ground, whatever they say over the ridge'), with Rosalie's cheese-vat disproof of the watering charge
Rosalie the daughter, ran the factory after him, Alder Corners figures copied out by her for Ivy in 1958
Section A names Strawn and his 1936 retirement only; the Ordell circuit, the 1907 start, the notebook-a-year and his disinterest appear only in E19/F2, outside A
No lactometer anywhere in the eight reconstructions; the clean water checks 1907-1936 are argued only in F2
Story 2: on 12 June 1923 the state dairy inspector ran the pipettes against a burette and condemned the whole crate
Nothing in Section A on his writing no figure for the deficiency and making no report beyond the condemnation

Replacement ordered 28 June and Ammon's letter of 2 July are in Story 2, but the 1924 average of 3.80 - this item's own aspect, the average that followed - appears only in C1(b), D2 and F1, never inside Section A
Crate in the station loft; notebooks to the state office in 1936 and to the Farland college library in 1947, where Ivy found them
'The patrons petitioned in January 1925' - the date carries the item
Board under Alonzo Frick, first session 17 March 1925, award 4 May, three sessions, second and third in the station's own weigh room
Water (Vose), theft by the tester (Teague), the hay (1908 report read in) - all three put, none accepted
Four books listed, including the inspector's 1923 circuit notebook containing the condemnation, with Kyle's line about nobody laying the second beside the fourth
Put out 30 April 1925 with no finding ever made against him; award 4 May 1925, $3,800, without admission, charged to the station account

Section A never states that $3,800 was one fifth of the $19,000 lost, nor that the award was charged to the very account the loss had been accumulating in as 'gain'; the one-fifth calculation lives only in C1(d)
Ivy b.1931, Duncan's daughter and Ansel's granddaughter, graduate work in dairy husbandry at Farland, bulletin with Professor Leland Vaught
Five sets of records put in one room: test book, Brant weigh book, Alder Corners figures, Strawn's notebooks, Association ledgers
February 1958, up the nailed ladder into the loft, crate stencilled AMMON & SONS, nine pipettes survived unbroken
9 March 1958, calibrated burette at Farland, every stem blown 17.6, mean 16.72 c.c., 0.95 of the mark, one part in twenty short
1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 low by one part in twenty (bulletin quote), 3.61 for 3.80, 0.19, and the error stated as proportional rather than a fixed offset

REQUIRED four elements are not all inside Section A: 76,000 lb and the ledger identity are there (bulletin quote), but neither the 40,000,000 lb (nor 1,600,000 x 25 years) nor the $19,000 appears anywhere in the eight reconstructions - both live only in Section C
Bulletin No. 471, Farland, October 1958, clears him; thirty-five years after the condemnation, twenty-four years dead
Granddaughter
Derivation via Duncan; notes Falke's own appended retraction of 'great-niece' and the dependency of the two carriers
Second cousins, derived: Orra and Emmet siblings, Duncan and Roy first cousins, their daughters second cousins

A08 asserted: 'I take them for full siblings on the weight of three sources' and E25 'Resolved to full siblings' - a verdict sentence with no declining qualifier, despite the 'sources leave open' framing. It does correctly note the degree is unaffected either way, but the abstention point is lost
Son; the 'nephew' carriers named and outweighed by the officer list, Vose's own words, Duncan and Kyle
Significance given both ways: Gideon wrote Article VII making the station's test decisive, and the 4.56 Jersey herd was his father's and lost the most per hundredweight
Correct abstention: no kinship established, 'not that kinship is disproved'
What is established: two self-labelled hearsay claims naming no link, probably one rumour twice, against a single family denial - 'a negative resting on one witness'
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, 95 per cent of true, 5 per cent short, proportional not an offset
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80, short 0.19 of a point
76,000 lb, with the 1,520,000 - 1,444,000 route and the 3,040 x 25 ledger cross-check
$19,000 at 25c, award $3,800, 3,800/19,000 = 0.20, one fifth; money and fraction both given
$86.40 at Roy Brant's 1910 price of 24c, given as the better answer with $90.00 flagged as the period average
1,444,000 lb credited
1,520,000 lb delivered in the cream
5.00% of fat delivered and 5.26% of fat credited, denominators named explicitly and the 'of the true fat' version rejected as wrong
$77.93 with the five line items summed
72 pipettes (six dozen), each short 17.6 - 16.72 = 0.88 c.c.

Exact-match failure on the duration: '26 years, 1 month and 12 days'. The key's answer is 26 years and 6 weeks / 42 days / 26 years 1 month 11 days, and 12 days is not an exact equivalent. The 25 full delivery years 1898-1922 and the part-year reason are both correct
A02 correctly abstained: no 1896 intake figure in any book, the ~900,000 and 1,100,000 figures are hearsay of lost sheets with nothing to discriminate
Variable named: the glass vessel that measured the charge, the station's own pipette replaced and then restored
Constants: same families and herds, same ground and pasture, same scale, same acid, bottles and hand tester, same operator, same book
3.80 held for nine weeks and fell back to 3.61 on 10 July, the day the station's own measure returned

Both halves: single-variable intervention with return to baseline defeating herd/ground/feed/men at once, plus explicit limits (which instrument was right, size in other years, all 72 pipettes, cause of the shortness, the lender immaterial)
Four distinct reasons attributed across Sill, the station test book / Strawn's notebook, Vaught's mechanism and Rundle
Independence argued, with the honest caution that Sill's book and the ledger column are one fact recorded twice; Reason 1 and the 1911/1924 halves named as holding without the 1958 measurement
A09 asserted: bold headline 'Did the bookkeeper ever question those entries? No.', with Teague's 1916 approach to Vose taken as fact; no declared inability to settle
Literal question answered yes, with the 1902 complaints, the 1919 circular and the 1926 address
REQUIRED three of five met: manager from 1913, signed the annual sheet carrying the station-gain line, wrote the 1919 circular, argued water at the hearing

A03 asserted: 'he knew the fat did not reconcile ... the answer is still yes', resting it on the station-gain sheets and Teague's 1916 report, plus a positive verdict the other way on the glass ('good evidence he did not'). This is the understatement question the key requires to be declined

Capped at 3; far more than three rows found, correctly resolved and methoded (weigh book 1 Jan 1897 on the exhibit list, six farms, Vose manager 1913 on the officer list, Strawn 1907 on his own note, 1924 average 3.80, the 1908 three-month sampling, crate in the loft, Ammon in Ordell before 1900, Nym's swapped attributions, 1908 committee vs 1925 board, Keddie's start). Misses: the circular's reach (leans wrongly to eleven, hedged), the station-gain origin (left unresolved), Alder Corners founding (resolved wrongly to 1913)

Capped at 3; explicit TWO-WRONG pairs with breakers named - 16.27 (NT-1, arithmetic against the observed 3.80), $77.39 (NT-14, summing the carrier's own facsimile), eleven pipettes (NT-16), five dozen (NT-15), 12 July (NT-11), the 5.26% denominator (NT-20), six weeks (NT-12), great-niece, first-cousin-once-removed, nephew

A06 earned ('cannot be settled', Strawn's notebook would decide it, immaterial to the result) and A10 earned ('cannot be firmly established', undated by-laws, minute book lost in the 1938 move, the text itself certain). A04 not earned: the short lot is leaned to accident ('most probably a reground mold') and the substitution pole called unsupported, with no statement that the sources cannot settle it

Nine self-refutations catalogued explicitly (Vaught's 16.27 body against his own conclusion, Grigg's letter against the report beneath it, Ammon's prose against her own facsimile, Teague's 1905 against an 1898 entry, Rundle, Falke, the Chronicle)
Buckets sum to 9; the key caps Section E at 8

Cause and size fully derived: the 1897 Ammon pipettes, 16.72 against a marked 17.6, 0.95 on a neck ruled in per cent, 0.19 as 5 per cent of 3.80 and not a constant, onset 1 May 1897 and cessation 12 June 1923 with nothing on the farms changing at either end
Watering named (Vose's 1919 circular and 1926 address) and defeated by Strawn's lactometer, the cheese vat, the 1908 water inquiry, the flatness of the gap and the 1924 rise

Theft named (Teague, the valley, Oram's father) and defeated by the cream arriving heavy on Sill's own weighing, the station-gain line, 1911 and 1924 with the same man at the bench, and the intake-sample mechanism

Bog hay named (Grigg's 1908 committee, Kepp, Falke's concession) and defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer, the three-month sampling, and the Alder Corners figures

A07 asserted: bold headline 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No.' The supporting observations are right, but the verdict is stated in the sheet's own voice with no declination
A05 asserted: the two uncorroborated recollections resolved into a chronology (glass in 1911, patrons by 1925) and concluded 'it is true that he accused nobody, and false that he suspected nobody'
140 words counted across both paragraphs, within the 150 cap
Five or more record series named: the ledger, the outside cheese factory, the inspector, the weigh book, the hearing, plus the 1958 measurement of the condemned glass
REQUIRED met: no decoy adopted (water/theft/hay appear only as who blamed whom) and every headline number right - 17.6, 16.72, 3.61/3.80, 76,000 lb, $19,000, $3,800
REQUIRED four of six covering both ends: five per cent / one part in twenty and 1897 at the onset, 76,000 lb and $19,000, 1958 at the close, Ansel Keddie named (Ivy only as 'his granddaughter')

deductions.reason: Corruption: the station-gain line asserted as Teague's own invention of 1905 (Story 5, 'In 1905 Wilbur Teague ... invented at his own desk a line'; repeated flatly in D2), where the ledger carried it from 1898; E39's later hedge does not undo the assertion
Corruption: Alder Corners asserted as built by Cudd in 1913 (Story 6; E21 resolves to 'Cudd'). The key permits 1914 or a declared unreconcilable, but asserting 1913 as fact takes the deduction
Corruption: 'Fourteen overlapping seasons' asserted in Story 8, contradicting the run's own correct sixteen seasons 1915-1930 in Story 6; the fourteen-season overlap is a catalogued planted error
Gullibility: A08 asserted - Orra and Emmet resolved to full siblings ('I take them for full siblings'; E25 'Resolved to full siblings')
Gullibility: A09 asserted - 'Did the bookkeeper ever question those entries? No.'
Gullibility: A03 asserted - Vose 'knew the fat did not reconcile ... the answer is still yes', plus a positive verdict that he did not know the glass was short
Gullibility: A07 asserted - 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No.'
Gullibility: A05 asserted - the tester's private belief resolved chronologically, 'false that he suspected nobody'
